title: The 5 Most Common Cells in Your Body, Ranked (Brain Cells Miss Out)

scenes.text: The five most common cells in your body. Your 86 billion brain cells don't even make the list.
Number five: lymphocytes, your immune cells. About 450 billion of them, one and a half percent of you, hunting infections.
scenes.label: Lymphocytes · 450 billion

scenes.text: Number four: the cells lining your blood vessels. About 600 billion, tiling roughly 100,000 kilometres of pipe from the inside.
scenes.label: Vessel lining · 600 billion

scenes.text: Number three: bone marrow cells. About 750 billion, a factory pushing out around two million blood cells every second.
scenes.label: Bone marrow · 750 billion

scenes.text: Number two: platelets. About 1.5 trillion. Technically cell fragments, but they count, and they've plugged every cut you've ever had.
scenes.label: Platelets · 1.5 trillion

scenes.text: Number one: red blood cells. About 25 trillion, 84 percent of every cell in you. And still outnumbered: your gut carries around 38 trillion bacteria.
scenes.label: Red blood cells · 25 trillion

description:
The five most numerous cell types in an adult human body, ranked by count.
A 2016 study in PLOS Biology (Sender, Fuchs and Milo) put the total at about 30 trillion human cells: roughly 25 trillion red blood cells (84%), 1.5 trillion platelets, 750 billion bone marrow cells, 600 billion vascular endothelial cells and 450 billion lymphocytes. Neurons and glia together are under one percent. The same study estimated about 38 trillion bacteria in the body, most in the gut.
Which of these surprised you most, and what should we rank next?
first_comment: Count your cells and you are 84 percent blood. Weigh them and you are mostly muscle and fat. Which would you put at number one, and what should we rank next?
